title: The PERFECT Chest Workout by Athlean-X Review
summary: NH reviews Athlean-X's 'perfect chest workout': four pressing movements (bench, incline, weighted dip, weighted push-up), each paired with crossovers at 4x6-12. He calls it a terrible bro-split program: so much volume that it can't be done with real intensity, it doesn't prioritise strength work, and it can't be progressively overloaded. His fix is to cut half of it and spend the time on other muscles.
claims: Body-part splits, especially a whole day for the chest, are a poor way to train
Splitting the chest into upper/middle/lower areas creates an 'isolationist mindset' that misses the big picture: compound movements that build quality tonnage fast
Full range of motion isn't automatically better; partials have their place, but with the same weight a deeper range is harder
A program should stand on its own, not hide behind long scientific introductions
Open a press day with a vertical or horizontal press
Evolving rep ranges work because you aren't bound to a fixed number; prescribing a fixed 12-10-8-6 sequence removes their benefit
4 sets for the chest is relatively high volume and fine by itself
Strength work should be the priority; light pre-activation is fine, but nothing that fatigues the main lift
Bench plus incline at 4 sets each is already enough chest work for the session
Programs with too many exercises prevent you from pushing intensity, so people sandbag and produce junk volume
Four horizontal presses in one session is more chest volume than most people need in a week
Better version: one main press (bench, weighted dip or push-up) for 4 sets of evolving reps to failure, then 4 sets of incline supersetted with crossovers
Use the time saved for lateral raises, face pulls, forearms and biceps; pressing-heavy sessions need balancing
With four similar presses you can't progressively overload: improving one hurts the others
Athlean-X's biggest problem is that he doesn't know how to program for size or strength
Spending 90 minutes pumping your chest gives no results
exercises: best opener for a press day
squeeze movement; fine after the press, but before it would hurt bench performance
upper chest; hybrid of vertical and horizontal pressing
